$comment: MACHINE half of the responder's pre-session gates (agents/coordinator/responder-argo.yaml respond; agents/responder-budget.sh); the HUMAN half is responder-gates.md. Spike (2026-11-07): the shell reads these shapes with jq/grep; nothing imports this file.

payload_alert.description: one member of the Alertmanager webhook payload's `alerts` (the Sensor passes the body verbatim as the `payload` parameter)

triage.description: the route sends only `now`; the in-pod belt re-checks

subject.description: the failing object — the cascade in the >>>REPLAY:responder-subject>>> block, first match wins, shared with the dig

ledger.$comment: keys: fp-<fp> (per fingerprint), subj-<sha256(alertname|subject)[:16]> (per subject), spawn-<date>-<fp> (write-once); values as below

^spawn-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-.description: WRITE-ONCE, one per spawned session — the budget's count; earlier days pruned

^fp-.description: `<date>|<incident>` (or `<date>|grouped:<leader fp>`) = triaged today; the prefixed values are markers that satisfy no dedup and consume no budget

budget_gauges.description: pushgateway job responder_budget — pushed on both paths

responder_triage_probe_ok.description: 0 = the ledger exists but could not be read — blocked fail-closed

responder_triage_day_start.description: 00:00Z of the day the numbers describe

still_firing_line.pattern: ^still-firing: .+ — .+ is still firing on this subject \(alert-fp:[0-9a-f]+\)\. Already triaged; the verdict above stands until this issue closes\.$
still_firing_line.description: the ONE line a decided re-fire rewrites in the existing issue body

declared_window.description: one value of the responder-window ConfigMap (written by agents/seat-window.sh)

alerts.description: alert NAMES — matched by name alone, never namespace

tail_until.description: a closed window still owns what it named until here
